["When evaluating a chest radiograph for suspected congenital lung anomalies, check for the triad of unilateral volume loss, ipsilateral mediastinal shift, and compensatory hyperaeration of adjacent lobes. Specifically, look for vascular anomalies such as a 'kinked' vessel in the cardiophrenic angle, which may indicate pulmonary hypoplasia or agenesis rather than simple atelectasis. This check applies when differentiating between acquired collapse (atelectasis) and developmental defects (hypoplasia/agenesis). Available tools are insufficient if they provide only binary 'normal/abnormal' classifications without anatomical localization or if automated reports fail to identify subtle vascular contours and lobar volume discrepancies, requiring direct visual inspection of the original image.", "When reviewing chest radiographs for acute clinical changes, specifically suspected pneumothorax, check for the presence of a visceral pleural line separated from the chest wall by a radiolucent space devoid of lung markings. This check applies when a patient presents with sudden onset pleuritic pain, dyspnea, or asymmetric breath sounds, particularly in the context of underlying lung disease or mechanical ventilation. However, available tools are insufficient if they provide only single-image analysis without calibrated probability scores or if they cannot perform direct side-by-side temporal comparison; automated classifiers may miss subtle pneumothoraces (yielding 'no strong finding' rather than 'normal'), and single-image reports cannot establish chronological evolution or distinguish new pathology from baseline abnormalities without explicit timepoint binding."]
